title: Post’s theorem and the hierarchy of oracle power

based_on.title: Computability theory
based_on.pages: Version 2024-02-25; §16.1, printed/PDF pp.68–69: finite-oracle absorption, Post’s theorem, strictness and completeness; with the wrong oracle in Lemma16.5(5) corrected

summary: Finite quantifier alternations correspond exactly to recognition and decision using successive Turing jumps.
abstract: An extra alternation of numerical quantifiers and an extra halting oracle are two ways to increase the power of a definition. Post’s theorem identifies their exact relationship. A set at the next existential level is precisely one whose members can be recognized using the corresponding finite jump of the original oracle; having both existential and universal descriptions gives a decision procedure using that same jump. The proof replaces each successful oracle run by a finite, ordinarily checkable bounded computation and a condition saying that its guessed oracle answers are correct. This connects computation to the quantifier classes without defining those classes by oracle power. The theorem supplies complete sets and proves that the positive levels are distinct, while the computable base and the first ambiguous level coincide. It also characterizes arithmetical sets as those decidable using some finite iterate of the ordinary halting oracle.
